messages:
jordan: Customer ticket #4256 — prod decrypts started failing ~10:45 UTC after key rotation. Customer sees AccessDeniedException from our API when we call KMS Decrypt. They say writes succeeded, only decrypts failing. Stack trace attached: `com.redwood.api.kms.DecryptException: AccessDenied`

sam: Can you paste the KMS Key ARN and the exact API call you make? Need to repro in staging. Also any encryptionContext they pass?

jordan: Key ARN: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345
jordan: API: we call our service which calls AWS KMS Decrypt with CiphertextBlob from S3, and we set encryptionContext {"app":"customerX","env":"prod"} when encrypting. Customer says after rotation they didn't change anything on their side.

sam: Got it. Trying a local repro with the ciphertext they provided. Quick check: CloudTrail shows a kms:Decrypt attempt at 10:45 with error: "AccessDeniedException: User not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key". Important: KMS supports conditions on EncryptionContext — the key policy or IAM may require specific keys to be present.

carmen: I'm looking at the CMK policy. There's a Condition block requiring `kms:EncryptionContext:app` == "customerX". If the decrypt call omits encryptionContext or has a different key casing, KMS will deny. Also some SDKs omit the encryption context accidentally when decrypting if they use different helper layers.

mike: Also check for mismatch in bytes-vs-string: encryption context values are case-sensitive string keys. If the application re-serializes the context (e.g., single vs double quotes) it might differ. We saw this before with the Go SDK wrapper.

jordan: Customer insists they pass the same context. I've asked them to copy the exact HTTP payload. They sent this snippet from their service logs: `{"CiphertextBlob":"<base64>", "EncryptionContext":{}}` — oh. Their decrypt payload is an empty object. Encrypt had context, decrypt call missing it.

sam: That explains it. Two remediation paths: 1) customer updates their service to include the same EncryptionContext on decrypt; or 2) they relax the CMK policy to not require EncryptionContext (not recommended unless they accept risk). For a quick unblock we can create a one-off KMS grant that allows Decrypt for their principal without the condition.

carmen: Policy snippet (current) that enforces the requirement:
```json
{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/service-role"},"Action":"kms:Decrypt","Resource":"*","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"kms:EncryptionContext:app":"customerX"}}}
```

sam: To repro locally I called: 
```bash
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --key-id arn:aws:kms:... --encryption-context app=customerX env=prod
```
If I omit `--encryption-context` I get AccessDenied; with it, decrypt succeeds and returns Plaintext.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] KMS key rotation job completed for key/abcd-ef01-2345 at 2026-02-12T10:40:01Z :white_check_mark:

jordan: Customer rotated the key earlier today (auto-rotate ON). Their code path for decrypt had a fallback that accidentally strips context when a certain optimization kicks in — they just confirmed the bug. They patched and pushed a fix to prod at 11:02 UTC.

mike: Action items: 
- jordan: confirm customer decrypts now succeed end-to-end and close ticket if green.
- sam: add a detection rule in our gateway logs to surface Decrypt AccessDenied errors that mention EncryptionContext mismatch (search for KMS AccessDenied + empty context).
- carmen: recommend guidance for customers on rotation: remind to always pass same EncryptionContext for encrypt/decrypt and include example SDK usage in docs.

carmen: Doc snippet suggestion to include: 
"When using an encryption context at encrypt time, you must supply the same context when calling Decrypt. Example (AWS CLI): `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --encryption-context app=customerX`"

jordan: Customer confirms: after patch, decrypts pass. We asked them to run a sweep for other codepaths that might omit context. They also set a CloudWatch alarm if kms:Decrypt denies exceed 5/min.

sam: I'll follow up with a small postmortem and a short note for support runbook: how to triage KMS Decrypt AccessDenied (check CloudTrail -> key policy -> encryptionContext -> SDK wrapper).

jordan: Closing loop — ticket updated, customer notified. Marking as resolved unless we see recurrence. :thumbsup:

mike: Thanks everyone. Leaving a pointer for eng docs: add a troubleshooting checklist item about encryption context and grants.
